subject: Proposed burst carveout and measurement ops playbook for p50/p95 windows
messages:
From: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finityhealth.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finityhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted p50/p95 measurement during seasonal surge - ask

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare our procurement package, two things came up from our ops and legal teams:

1) We want to lock p50/p95 latency commitments for the hosted API in the contract, but we need a clear operational definition of the measurement windows (how quantiles are computed, sampling cadence, and handling of transient bursts).
2) During our October open-enrollment period we expect a sustained 6-8x traffic spike for ~72 hours. We need a proposal for how Redwood will treat that burst for p95 calculations (temporary carveout, padding, or other mitigation) and the evidence we should provide to our auditors to support any exception.

Could you share a concrete proposal (playbook + checklist) that we can include in the SOW? Also note procurement asked for supporting artifacts they can attach to the contract (measurement checklist, logging requirements, and a template for an exception window).

Best,
Amelia Johnson
VP Ops, Finity Health

Attachments: none (will accept Redwoods materials)

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finityhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted p50/p95 measurement during seasonal surge - ask

Amelia —

Thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short playbook and a checklist; please find the two attachments we usually share for procurement: redwood_burst_carveout_proposal.pdf and measurement_ops_checklist.xlsx. High-level summary below so your auditors get the gist quickly: 

- Measurement windows: We compute p50/p95 on 1-minute rolling windows aggregated into a 24-hour epoch for contract compliance. The primary contracted metric is the 24-hour epoch p95.
- Burst treatment: For planned, predictable bursts (you flagged Oct open-enrollment), we can offer a temporary, time-boxed carveout that excludes the core 72-hour burst window from contractual p95 calculation if both parties confirm the window 7 days in advance and agree on an evidence package post-window. The carveout is limited (max 2 carveouts/year per account) and excludes unplanned incidents.
- Evidence & ops items we provide: request/approval email thread, CDN & request-level histograms, token-level latency distributions, service-side tracing for the window, and a playback of routing decisions. We also include an auto-rollover mitigation plan (burst routing to Dedicated capacity or permissive model variants) if configured.

Next steps: if you like this framing, I can add specific acceptance criteria that map to the SLA language your legal team would use. Lauren, Ben — please review the attachment wording and confirm we can commit to the 7-day notice and max 2 carveouts limit.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_burst_carveout_proposal.pdf, measurement_ops_checklist.xlsx

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-30T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Proposed carveout wording + evidence checklist

Rafa — quick internal note for the thread (will keep Finity copied once we finalize):

I reviewed the draft playbook. Two suggested clarifications before we send a contract-ready paragraph:

1) Define "planned burst" precisely: propose language -> a planned burst is any traffic increase where 7+ days notice is provided and the window is declared and signed off by both parties. We limit to 72 continuous hours or fewer per carveout; anything longer triggers a capacity review and potential Dedicated recommendation.
2) Add a post-window evidence timeline: we commit to delivering the evidence package within 5 business days after the window closes. That gives Finity auditors the artifacts and gives our SREs time to collate traces and histograms.

Ben, can you confirm we can produce the artifacts listed in the checklist within 5 business days and that the two-carveout/year limit is safe operationally? Also flag anything that should be redactable for privacy/regulatory reasons (PHI-safe guidance).

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Solutions

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-02T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Proposed carveout wording + evidence checklist

Lauren / Rafa — confirmed. Operational notes for the contract paragraph: 

- Artifacts: we can produce request-level latency histograms, KV cache hit-rate summaries, trace samplings, and token-level latency distributions. All artifacts can be sanitized to remove PII/PHI; however, if customers request full traces that include user content, that falls under an elevated access request and will require a signed Data Handling Addendum.
- Timing: 5 business days to deliver the evidence package is achievable if the window is tagged at the start and our incident-runbook tasks are followed. We recommend including an SLA clause that states Redwood will deliver the evidence package within 5 business days of request for planned carveouts, and within 10 business days for unplanned incidents (where available).
- Limits: two planned carveouts per 12-month period is operationally reasonable. For prolonged or recurring seasonal traffic, we should recommend Dedicated or autoscaling burst credits in the SOW rather than repeated carveouts.

I can rework the draft paragraph into redline-ready language for legal. Let me know and I'll loop Legal.

-Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
